title: hivemind_find returns 0 results for every query despite 13 stored memories with embeddings
description:
hivemind_stats reports: memories 13, embeddings 13, healthy true, ollama_available true, all 13 chunks under collection "opencode-swarm". So storage is working.

But hivemind_find returns {"results": [], "count": 0} for EVERY query tried, including single-word queries that must match stored content: "moonrepo", "kata", "template", and "moon template tera interpolation kata bun". Workers in this epic explicitly stored moon/Tera/template learnings that these queries should hit.

Impact: this is severe and silent. Every swarm worker prompt mandates "query hivemind BEFORE writing any code". Workers run the query, get 0 results, correctly conclude "no prior art", and proceed — so the failure looks identical to a genuinely greenfield repo. The swarm's collective memory is write-only: it accumulates learnings that can never be retrieved, and every agent repeats work the previous one already did.

Timeline note: at the start of this epic Ollama was down and hivemind_store failed outright (a researcher reported two failed attempts). Ollama is up now and stores succeed. So embedding generation recovered, but retrieval did not — suggesting the issue is in the query/similarity path rather than the embedding path. Possible leads: memories written while Ollama was down may have null/zero-vector embeddings inflating the count; or a similarity threshold that filters everything; or a collection-scoping mismatch (all chunks are under "opencode-swarm" while find may default to "default").

Repro: hivemind_stats (shows 13/13 healthy) then hivemind_find(query="kata", limit=10) -> 0 results.

Upstream fix: status default corruption lives in opencode-swarm-plugin bundle, not swarm-mail
description:
Durable follow-up to katas--w5hg2-mshn7z19q79, which was fixed only by patching compiled output in the global install. That patch is silently reverted by the next `bun install -g`.

ROOT CAUSE: Drizzle schema `db/schema/memory.ts` ~line 86 has `status: text("status").default("'active'")` — the default value contains literal single-quote characters, so every memory is written with the 7-char string 'active' instead of the 6-char active. store() never sets status explicitly, so all rows inherit it. search() and ftsSearch() then filter `WHERE (m.status IS NULL OR m.status = 'active')`, which never matches. Result: every query returns 0 results while stats reports a healthy corpus. Silent and total.

CRITICAL DISCOVERY — the obvious fix target is WRONG: patching ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/swarm-mail had ZERO effect. The hivemind_* MCP tools shell out to the `swarm` CLI, which resolves to ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/opencode-swarm-plugin/dist/bin/swarm.js — a separate, independently-bundled ~440K-line copy of the same swarm-mail logic. The plugin VENDORS its own copy. This was found only by testing store->find end-to-end and watching a brand-new memory get corrupted again after the first patch appeared to succeed. Any upstream fix that only touches swarm-mail will appear to work in isolation and change nothing in practice.

The bundle contained multiple copies: 1 schema default + 4 statusFilter occurrences (2 pairs from duplicate bundling) + 1 additional schema default in a third bundled copy. A fix must sweep all of them, or fix the source and rebuild the plugin bundle.

SCOPE OF DAMAGE: any memory written by any unpatched install is unreachable. The fix should (a) correct the schema default so new writes are clean, AND (b) widen the status filter to also accept the legacy corrupted value so previously-written rows stay searchable. Both. (b) alone leaves the corruption ongoing; (a) alone orphans existing memories.

Existing memories are fully recoverable with a metadata UPDATE — no re-embedding needed, embeddings are valid.

Source checkout at ~/.opencode-autopsy/joelhooks/swarm-tools has a partial fix (widened statusFilter + ANN-fallback exact scan) that was NEVER PUBLISHED — its package.json version 1.11.2 is identical to what npm serves and what is installed, so there is no version signal that a fix exists. The schema default is still wrong even there.

title: Migrate hivemind embeddings to MLX runner with nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (768-dim)
description:
NO-GO — verified by benchmark on M5 / 24GB, not inferred. Step 1 (katas--w5hg2-mshpacihhs2) closed with evidence:

1. nomic-embed-text-v1.5 has NO MLX build — verified against the HuggingFace API, not assumed. The entire rationale for that model (dual Ollama+MLX runtime enabling a clean A/B) evaporates. mlx-omni-server ended up running mlx-community/mxbai-embed-large-v1 — literally the same weights Ollama already serves.

2. No speed win. Warm median n=20: MLX 32.0ms vs Ollama 33.1ms. A wash.

3. RAM is WORSE: MLX resident ~1.26GB (fp32) vs Ollama ~686MB (F16 quantized).

4. Dependency bloat: "MLX-native" mlx-omni-server pulled torch, spacy, transformers, jieba — a 1.7GB venv for a local embedding call.

5. Matryoshka truncation is not implemented server-side — the `dimensions` request param exists in the schema but is never used in the code. Dimension is fixed at 1024 (counted, not trusted from docs).

THE ONE REAL FINDING: MLX cold start 366ms vs Ollama 7.96s. That gap is Ollama's idle model-unload, NOT an inherent MLX advantage — fixable with OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE. That is a one-line env change instead of a provider shim + schema migration F32_BLOB(1024)->768 + full re-embed + a second hand-patch of the 440K-line plugin bundle.

RECOMMENDATION: abandon the MLX swap, set OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE to keep mxbai-embed-large resident. Same benefit, none of the risk. Child steps 2 (katas--w5hg2-mshpafx6fq5) and 3 (katas--w5hg2-mshpah25r05) should be closed unless the user wants MLX for reasons beyond efficiency.

description: Third occurrence today of ~/.config/swarm-tools/swarm.db losing all memory data (memories:0, embeddings:0, healthy:true — total silent loss, not the earlier status-corruption issue). Investigated and restored. See closure notes for full report.

title: swarm.db has no single-writer arbitration — every tool call opens a fresh SQLite connection, causing SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY under concurrent swarms
description:
ROOT CAUSE of three swarm.db wipes on 2026-08-06 (last one 15:53, ~536KB empty-tables file, memories:0 embeddings:0 healthy:true).

ARCHITECTURE: hivemind_*/hive_* MCP tools shell out to the `swarm` CLI binary (~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/opencode-swarm-plugin/dist/bin/swarm.js) per invocation — every single tool call is a brand-new OS process that opens its own @libsql/client connection directly against the local WAL-mode file ~/.config/swarm-tools/swarm.db, does its work, and closes. There is no long-lived daemon/server holding a stable lock or serializing writes across concurrent agents.

EVIDENCE:
- logs/errors-2026-08-06.log shows SQLITE_BUSY and SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY on hive_close/hive_sync/hivemind_stats repeatedly across the whole afternoon (14:59, 15:42, 16:04, 16:59, 19:50), spanning well before and after the 15:53 wipe — this is a persistent, ongoing condition, not a one-off.
- SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY specifically means a connection found a hot/inconsistent WAL and couldn't complete recovery because another process held a conflicting lock — i.e., WAL recovery was actively contending, repeatedly, all day.
- Reproduced live during this recovery session: a single sequential hivemind_store() followed immediately by hivemind_find() (no other agents running, verified via `ps aux`) hit SQLITE_BUSY on the very next call. This is NOT purely a multi-agent problem — the per-call connection churn alone is enough to race the WAL/shm state.
- The last logged tool_call before the 15:53 wipe was hive_create at 15:52:04; nothing is logged again until 16:04:23. Whatever wrote empty tables to swarm.db during that gap did not go through the logged CLI tool-call path — consistent with a WAL checkpoint/recovery event resolving to an empty/stale snapshot rather than an explicit DROP TABLE.
- RULED OUT: dropLibSQLMemorySchema()/validateLibSQLMemorySchema() exist in the bundle (grep confirmed, dist/bin/swarm.js:11391) but are only ever invoked from unit tests in the source tree (schema-overhaul.test.ts, libsql-schema.test.ts, entity-extraction.test.ts) — never from any production code path in the CLI. Not the mechanism.
- RULED OUT: no cron/launchd job touches swarm.db (checked crontab -l and ~/Library/LaunchAgents). No swarm/libsql process was running at investigation time (safe window confirmed).
- RULED OUT: the status-corruption hand-patch work (upstream-patches/swarm-tools-hivemind-status-fix, applied ~15:17) explicitly did NOT touch the live global install or swarm.db per its own README — all work happened in scratch clones.

MECHANISM (best-supported hypothesis): many short-lived processes opening/closing WAL-mode SQLite connections against the same local file, with implicit auto-checkpoints racing live writers from other just-spawned processes, occasionally causes a checkpoint/recovery to complete against a truncated or stale page set — silently emptying tables while leaving schema intact (exactly the observed symptom: healthy:true, 0 rows, tables present).

PREVENTION (recommended, priority order):
1. Route all local swarm.db access through a single long-lived process (e.g. a local libSQL server / sqld, or an in-process singleton connection pool inside a persistent MCP server) instead of CLI-per-tool-call. This is the actual fix — everything else is mitigation.
2. If (1) isn't immediately feasible: set `PRAGMA busy_timeout` high (10000ms+) on every connection the CLI opens, and wrap every write path in retry-with-backoff on SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY (purge-garbage.ts already does this — the pattern should move into the shared CLI DB-open path, not stay script-local).
3. Add a scheduled (e.g. hourly, low-cost) automated backup rotation of swarm.db — the only reason this incident was recoverable three times is that manual/ad-hoc backups happened to exist. That should not be load-bearing.
4. Add a startup/periodic health check that does a real round-trip (store+find, not just stats) and alerts loudly on silent-empty state, since `healthy:true` with 0 rows is indistinguishable from "fresh install" today.
